sbar.situation: The incident is recovered and confirmed clean on two checks in a row. The gateway was restarted and the payments transfer limit was restored.
sbar.background: The gateway process stopped, so payment and balance requests timed out after 3.0s. A scheduler change 15 seconds before the fault set payments max_transfer_minor from 1000000 to 1, which would have rejected normal payments once traffic resumed. Payments traffic was 0.0/s against a baseline of 11.6/s, so the limit fault was hidden behind the gateway outage.
sbar.assessment: Root cause one: gateway process_down, confidence 0.95. Evidence showed the gateway not answering and no recent warnings or errors. The incident commander restarted the gateway, and it is running again. Root cause two: payments bad_config, confidence 0.85. The incident commander reverted max_transfer_minor from 1 to 1000000, and the value is restored. The screening-standby restarts were routine and were not faults.
sbar.recommendation: Find out why the scheduler changed max_transfer_minor to 1 and prevent it from happening again. Watch payments traffic for a return toward the 11.6/s baseline. Operations should review payments that were rejected or timed out during the outage and any balance requests that failed, since these may have financial or data effects. Nothing has been escalated.
